main_argument_chains.claim: A measured tread surface can be mapped to long-term traffic and material parameters through a hybrid wear-and-inversion workflow.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Use the recovered parameters only as bounded archaeological hypotheses until field validation is supplied.

main_argument_chains.claim: Repairs and daily traffic require mechanisms beyond one homogeneous long-run surface.
main_argument_chains.decision_consequence: Keep repair chronology and event-scale parameters explicit when interpreting wear layers.

warnings.warning: Equation (3) uses a sum indexed by dt even though N dt is already the event count; the discrete-to-continuous step is not derived rigorously.
Phi is printed as Phi(x;,N) in several places, leaving an empty argument and an unstable notation boundary.
Figure 4 retains the placeholder caption 'xxx', so its intended evidentiary role must be inferred from adjacent prose.
The model is repeatedly called a PDE while explicitly omitting diffusion and adjacent spatial coupling; it is a pointwise time update unless additional coupling is supplied.
Environmental wear is reduced to a constant beta without units, calibration data, or a check against weathering mechanisms.
The single-file body-center choice, Beta(4,4) assumption, and W-shaped depression description are not reconciled quantitatively.
Equation (17) previews a prior-augmented objective before the later likelihood and energy definitions, making the naming of E inconsistent across sections.
Algorithm 2 adds beta outside the Delta t multiplier even though Equation (19) multiplies the whole rate by Delta t.
Figure 12 retains the placeholder caption 'xxx' and the prose cites unresolved equation references '(??)'.
The heuristic step says it minimizes E(Theta), while the stated MAP objective is -ln p(Theta)+E(Theta); prior handling in PSO is therefore ambiguous.
The inversion uses observations generated by the same forward model, so parameter recovery is an internal synthetic test rather than external validation.
The reported posterior has one 10000-step Metropolis-Hastings run with no acceptance rate, multi-chain comparison, autocorrelation, or effective sample size.
Table 2 labels 90% intervals but reports posterior mean +/- interval without stating whether the value is a half-width or asymmetric quantile range.
Layer exposure and wear-through are described locally at (x,y), but the switching procedure also speaks of a single top layer; local versus global activation is not formalized.
The QR advertisement touches the right side of Equation (26), creating a mild source-overlay risk near its final terms and number.
The nonhomogeneous arrival peaks in Equation (27) have no fitted data, units, or identifiability discussion.
The event wear factor eta_e and footprint normalization are not calibrated to physical depth, so the one-day field has an unresolved scale.
Figure 14 and the prose do not provide a reproducible parameter grid or raw curves for all short-term and long-term sensitivity claims.
The claimed +/-5% to +/-10% task uncertainties in the summary are not consistently tied to Table 2's intervals or a common confidence definition.
No real staircase holdout, repair chronology, material assay, or raw scan is used to validate the integrated pipeline.

visualization_dispositions.analytical_purpose: Connects the archaeological need, model sequence, inversion workflow, task-level numerical claims, advanced extensions, and stability claim.
Exposes the complete section hierarchy and the intended progression from preparation through sensitivity and limitations.
Establishes the observable concave wear pattern that motivates inference from stair geometry.
Maps data preparation, hybrid forward model, inverse estimation, extensions, and decision outputs.
Binds the core wear, traffic, footprint, and Bayesian notation before model construction.
Shows the scanning geometry that converts a tread into registered point-cloud and grid measurements.
Illustrates the micro-sliding interpretation used to connect pedestrian contact to Archard wear; the source caption remains 'xxx'.
Contrasts single-peak and double-peak wear fields and their qualitative stair profiles.
Compares short-term large-use and long-term small-use temporal fields and final cross-sections.
Locates front-foot ascent contact and rear-foot descent contact on stair geometry.
Visualizes the front/rear two-thirds masks used by the directional model.
Show four-time-step 3D evolution for ascending and descending wear.
Places ascent and descent surfaces side by side to support the directional comparison.
Shows a cloud-like inversion illustration, but the source caption remains 'xxx' and does not identify the encoded variables.
Traces forward simulation, measurement, prior, likelihood, smoothing, posterior, PSO, local MCMC, and reported results.
Reports true values, posterior means, intervals, and relative errors for material, age, logistic, and traffic parameters.
Compares wear curves under changes in kappa and alpha_short, with small but readable axes and labels.
Confirms that references [2]-[8] continue on the final page and that the reference list is not truncated.
